It connects real NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band radar observations with mapped infrastructure corridors, using the Kalka–Shimla Railway in India as its demonstration case. The platform verifies spatial overlap between the railway and the radar product footprint, visualizes unwrapped phase, coherence, connected components and data validity, and allows users to inspect individual source-grid cells along the railway. In our current case, 1,471 of 1,478 railway-touched raster cells pass a defined quality screen. Rather than presenting unverified deformation claims, StrainLine makes radar observability, product provenance and scientific uncertainty accessible. It aims to make complex SAR evidence easier to explore, communicate and evaluate for future infrastructure research.
details:
STRAINLINE — Ground Context Intelligence

Overview

StrainLine is a geospatial radar-evidence inspection platform that makes satellite SAR observations easier to explore in the context of critical infrastructure.

For the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge "Dancing with the SARs", we developed a working prototype using an actual NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band Geocoded Unwrapped Interferogram (GUNW) product over the Kalka–Shimla Railway in Himachal Pradesh, India.

How it works

The platform follows an evidence-based workflow:

  1. Corridor Selection: Users load an infrastructure alignment using an attributed GeoJSON file.
  2. NISAR Data Discovery: The application searches satellite-product metadata and displays acquisition information.
  3. Spatial Verification: It checks the railway geometry against the actual NISAR product footprint.
  4. Radar Visualization: It presents four actual data layers — unwrapped phase, coherence, connected components and combined validity.
  5. Source-Cell Inspection: Users select a railway location or raster cell and inspect synchronized full-resolution source-grid values, coordinates, phase, coherence, mask and subswath information.
  6. Provenance and Quality Review: Product identity, acquisition details, maturity, quality indicators and scientific limitations remain visible.

Real-data implementation

Our demonstration uses NISAR granule G4375022208-ASF, an L-band HH ascending, left-looking GUNW product with an 80 m posting. Its reference and secondary acquisitions are 4 October 2026 and 16 October 2026.

The mapped railway centreline touches 1,478 raster cells. Of these, 1,471 pass our documented combined phase, coherence, connected-component, subswath and anomaly screen (99.53%). Seven cells fail because their secondary subswath code is zero.

These results describe radar observability under the specified screen, not railway movement or track-level coverage.

What makes StrainLine different?

Instead of turning radar measurements into unsupported damage or risk scores, StrainLine allows users to inspect the underlying observations and their quality limitations. It connects infrastructure geometry, satellite-product provenance, spatial verification and source-cell-level evidence in one interactive interface.

The platform explicitly preserves unresolved product QA issues, phase-sign uncertainty and the absence of date-matched local GNSS validation. It does not claim validated displacement, railway settlement, structural damage or safety classification.

Technology stack

  • Python 3.11
  • FastAPI and Uvicorn
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • Leaflet for interactive mapping
  • NumPy and h5py for scientific data handling
  • Rasterio for geospatial raster processing
  • Shapely and PyProj for spatial geometry and coordinate transformations
  • Earthaccess and NASA Common Metadata Repository workflows for data discovery and access

Intended impact

StrainLine provides an accessible, reproducible way to investigate satellite radar evidence along infrastructure corridors. Its longer-term direction is to support scientifically validated multi-date change analysis using compatible observations and independent ground measurements.

Our guiding principle:

Inspect the signal. Verify the evidence. Understand the uncertainty.
